primary.title: US Thanksgiving air travel to hit 16-yr high
primary.description: Millions of Americans are expected to take to the skies for the Thanksgiving holiday this year, pushing scheduled air traffic to a 16-year high, with more than 417,000 flights set to operate over the nine-day travel period, according to the US Department of Transportation.November 25 is expected to be the busiest day, with over 52,000 flights scheduled. The projected number of services marks a sharp rise from last year's holiday period, when airlines had scheduled more than 360,000 flights.Also Read: Ancient Roman library reopens in Rome after nearly a century, offering visitors a glimpse into its historyThe surge in travel demand comes amid a series of technical problems that have disrupted airline operations across the country. Earlier this month, a failure in the air traffic control system forced a nationwide halt to flights, leading to the cancellation of around 20,000 services.United Airlines subsequently faced a separate technical breakdown that disrupted its systems for four hours. On Sunday, Delta Air Lines temporarily stopped departures from its Atlanta hub after another technology-related disruption triggered delays and cancellations.Also Read: Dubai airport handles 50.4 million passengers in 2026; India remains its biggest market despite regional disruptionThe US administration has sought to assure passengers that measures are being taken to maintain safe and reliable operations.Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy in a statement said, "The Trump Administration’s message is clear: your safety is our number one priority. The American people can rest assured we will continue to work around the clock 24/7 to get families where they need to go."Duffy has also called for $50 billion in emergency funding to replace and upgrade ageing air traffic control equipment.
